For r<=1 each rhombus gives a π/3 disk sector, resulting F=πr²/(3√3). For 1<r<√3 the complement comprises four equal corner triangles minus circular segments with t=(3−√(4r²−3))/2 and s=√3(1−t/2), giving the stated arccosine branch. Barycentric second moments on top/bottom faces are 5/12,17/12 hence E[R²]=11/12; differentiating gives F″ jump −4, and radial expansion at S yields tail (2/3)ε². Independent face-grid CDF computations agree. Universal proof is geometric.
